name: AccelDiff SADA step skipping
plain: Forks core solvers and adds a stability test: after each step it compares the real next state against a three-term predictor, and if a momentum indicator is non-positive it skips the next model call. The skipped call uses an extrapolated x0 or a Lagrange fit over stored x0 anchors. It trades model calls for approximation error.
math:
f = (x−x0)/σ. pred = x + Δσ·(0.625 f + 0.75 f₋₁ − 0.375 f₋₂). residual = x_next − pred. accel = (f−f₋₁) − (f₋₁−f₋₂). momentum = mean(residual·accel).
Skip next call if momentum ≤ 0 and acc_start ≤ i < acc_end, at most max_interval in a row. Replacement x0 = pred − σ_next·f, or Lagrange interpolation over lagrange_term stored x0 values once i ≥ lagrange_step (then skip when i % lagrange_int ≠ 0).
The base solver's update then runs unchanged on the substituted x0.

props.stages: 1 or fewer per step on skip; wrapped solver count otherwise

providers.author: jiajianxie
providers.note: Solvers forked: euler, heun, heunpp2 (SADA maps heunpp2 to heun), dpm_2, dpm_2_ancestral(+RF), lms, dpmpp_2m, euler_ancestral(+RF), deis, ipndm, ipndm_v, res_multistep, gradient_estimation

label: from code
surprise: Docstring gives Adams-Bashforth 23/12,−16/12,5/12, then says that simplifies to 0.625,0.75,−0.375; the two sets are not equal. Skipped steps' estimated f enters history here, unlike ZEUS.
